pages.title: A song chart for the session
pages.caption: The players already know their instruments. The bandleader still hands out a chart so everyone plays this song the same way. A skill is that chart. A custom agent is the specialist who follows it, with a defined role and the tools for the job. You still check the result.

pages.title: Choose the feature that fits
pages.caption: A one-off prompt lives in the current conversation and applies when you send it. Repository instructions (`.github/copilot-instructions.md`) apply across tasks in this project. A skill (`.github/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`) applies when the task matches its description or you invoke it. A custom agent (`.github/agents/<name>.agent.md`) applies when you select it with `/agent` or the agent picker.

pages.title: A one-off prompt or a skill?
pages.caption: Instructions are the house rules. A skill is the chart for one kind of song: a reusable checklist that lives in the repository and gives the same guidance each time. Use a skill when you repeat the same kind of work.

pages.title: Find skills in Customize
pages.caption: Select **Customize** in the sidebar, then the **Installed** tab. Set the type filter to **Skills** and search for `book-app-reviewer`: the result shows **Project: copilot-app-for-beginners**, and its toggle is on. You select custom agents with `/agent` or the agent picker in the prompt box.

pages.title: Install a skill
pages.caption: In **Customize**, select **Add**, then **Install skill…** You can install from a local folder, a ZIP file, a GitHub skill-folder URL or an HTTPS ZIP link. The app shows a review step before it writes anything to your machine, so you can check what the skill includes.

pages.title: Community skills and agents
pages.caption: After this chapter’s exercises, browse the Awesome Copilot directories for community agents and skills. Before you add or use another customization, review the agent’s tools or the skill’s instructions.

pages.title: A skill isn’t a lock
pages.caption: A skill tells Copilot how to approach a task, but its instructions don’t enforce what Copilot is allowed to do. A skill that says “review without editing” doesn’t disable file-editing tools. Skills can also include scripts or tell Copilot to use tools, so read unfamiliar skills before you turn them on. The course review skill contains instructions only.

pages.title: Your practice session
pages.caption: Select **Create from** next to your course project, then **Branches** and `main`, to start a session in a new worktree. Set the mode to **Interactive**, and keep this session for every exercise. File edits belong to this worktree, and a new worktree from `main` won’t contain them. Installed tools can have a wider scope.
pages.code: Show this session's branch and worktree path. Confirm that .github/skills/book-app-reviewer/SKILL.md and samples/book-app-web exist here. Do not edit files, commit, or push.

pages.title: A skill is a folder
pages.caption: A skill is a folder with a `SKILL.md` file. It starts with YAML frontmatter between two `---` lines: the `name`, and the `description` that helps the app decide when to load it. The Markdown below holds the instructions. Repository skills are shared through Git; personal skills apply across projects on your machine.
pages.code:
---
name: book-app-reviewer
description: Review changes in samples/book-app-web for accessibility, responsive layout, tests/build validation, and small beginner-safe changes.
---

pages.title: Update the skill
pages.caption: Ask Copilot to edit only `SKILL.md` and append two rules to Review focus: headings that describe the page structure, and text alternatives for informative images and icons. Inspect the **Changes** tab: only the two rules were added. Then submit `/skills reload` to load the edited skill.

pages.title: Use the skill
pages.caption: Set the mode to **Plan** and ask Copilot to use the `book-app-reviewer` skill on `@samples/book-app-web/src`. Expand the skill activity to confirm it loaded, and compare the plan with the rules in the file. If it moves book titles to `h3`, it must also account for the `.book-card h2` selector, and it mustn’t claim tests passed. Type `/` to find `/book-app-reviewer`.

pages.title: Hire the specialist
pages.caption: You don’t call one general helper for every repair: you call a plumber, an electrician or a roofer. A custom agent has a name, instructions and a set of available tools. A skill supplies a workflow; a custom agent defines the role that does the work. It isn’t a different session mode, or necessarily a different model.

pages.title: The agent profile
pages.caption: An agent profile is a Markdown file with YAML frontmatter, like a skill: `name` identifies it in the agent picker, `description` says what it’s for, `tools` limits the available tools (`read` and `search` inspect files without editing or running commands), and the Markdown below defines its behavior and answer format.
pages.code:
---
name: book-app-explainer
description: Explain the Book App's code and tests to a beginner without changing files.
tools: ["read", "search"]
---

pages.title: The read-only explainer
pages.caption: Create `.github/agents/book-app-explainer.agent.md` and check in **Changes** that `tools` holds only `read` and `search`. The app loads custom agents when it starts: wait for active work to finish, quit the app and open it again (closing the window isn’t quitting). Type `/agent`, select **book-app-explainer**, send it, and check the agent picker below the prompt box shows it.

pages.title: The toolbelt is the limit
pages.caption: The `tools` list limits the available tools; omitting it would allow all of them. The folder scope in the instructions guides the agent, but it isn’t a file-system sandbox. The explainer can’t run tests or save a report, on purpose: match an agent’s tools to its task, and use the default agent when you need those actions.

pages.title: Next-step suggestions
pages.caption: After a custom agent finishes its response, it may suggest next steps as a pre-filled prompt you can review and edit before you send it. Use one to switch to another agent, or carry on without retyping your intent.

pages.title: Key takeaways
pages.caption: Repository instructions give shared rules across a project; skills give reusable instructions for specific tasks. A custom agent defines a specialist role with its own instructions and tools: match its tools to its task. A skill supplies guidance, not a permission boundary. Don’t rely only on what Copilot says it did: check its activity and results against the files, and run the tests.

pages.title: Your skill-guided change
pages.caption: Take the skill’s heading recommendation (or a focused test) through the Chapter 03 inner loop: plan it with `/book-app-reviewer` in **Plan** mode, record a baseline in **Terminal**, build it in **Interactive**, check **Changes**, the tests, the build and the **Browser** at a wide and a narrow width, and save a review record of only what ran. Don’t commit or push.

pages.title: What’s next
pages.caption: You now have reusable review instructions and a small read-only agent. Chapter 05 extends what the app can access: an MCP server for documentation, and a plugin that supplies a reusable skill.

pages.title: A changed skill or new agent is missing?
pages.caption: Check the file is saved in this session’s worktree, and check its path and YAML frontmatter. For a skill, try `/skills reload`. For a new agent, or no reload command, let active work finish, then quit and reopen the app and return to the same session. Don’t start from `main` again.

pages.title: Generic advice?
pages.caption: Invoke the skill from the `/` menu, or name it. Expand the activity to see whether it loaded, and ask for file-specific evidence and the rules applied. Different wording alone doesn’t show whether the skill worked.

pages.title: Can’t find skills or custom agents?
pages.caption: Use the **Customize** view in the sidebar. Select custom agents with `/agent` or the agent picker in the prompt box. Labels and commands can vary by app version.

pages.title: The custom agent can’t run tests?
pages.caption: That’s on purpose: the example permits only reading and searching. Return to the default agent to run commands, and don’t add shell access just to make the read-only exercise work.

glossary.definition: A folder with a `SKILL.md` file of reusable instructions for one kind of task. The Copilot app loads it when the task matches its description, or when you invoke it. Find skills in **Customize**.
A specialist role with a name, instructions and a set of available tools, defined in an agent profile. Select one with `/agent` or the agent picker.
The block of metadata between two `---` lines at the top of a skill or agent file, such as its `name` and `description`.
The house rules in `.github/copilot-instructions.md`: shared guidance that applies across tasks in a project.
A Markdown file, `.github/agents/<name>.agent.md`, that defines a custom agent: `name`, `description`, `tools`, and its behavior below the frontmatter.
Below the prompt box when a custom agent is available: it shows the agent in use, and you can change it there or with `/agent`.
